** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The F-statistic is used to test the null hypothesis that the means of multiple groups are equal, versus the alternative hypothesis that at least one mean is different.
 
• The F-statistic follows an F-distribution with degrees of freedom (df) for the numerator (between treatments) and degrees of freedom for the denominator (error).
 
• The F-statistic is often used to determine if the variability between groups is significantly greater than the variability within groups.
 
• The decision to reject or fail to reject the null hypothesis depends on the F-statistic and the level of significance chosen by the researcher, which is often set at 0.05.
 
• The higher the F-statistic, the stronger the evidence against the null hypothesis, and in favor of the alternative hypothesis. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** **The **F-statistic** can be calculated as the ratio of the mean squares between treatments to the mean squares of error.
 
• The formula is:
 
 
• F = MS between / MS error
 
 
 
• where 
 
**MS between** = Sum of Squares between treatments / Degrees of Freedom between treatments

 
 
• 
 
**MS error** = Sum of Squares error / Degrees of Freedom error

 
 
• So, substituting the values from the question, we get:
 
• F = 75 / 3 / (48 / 16) = 75/3 * 16/48 = 25/16 = 8.33
 
• So the F-statistic is 8.33, which is option (a).
